name: equipment-documentation-v1
title: Equipment Documentation
description: Compare a specification, a maintenance guide, and a scanned inspection record for the fictional pump PMP-104.
provenance: Original fictional educational documents. Answers, graph relationships, and evidence references are manually authored, not live model output. All operating values are illustrative and must not be used for real equipment.

pages.title: PMP-104: Specification
pages.text:
The fictional pump PMP-104 has a rated pressure of 12 bar. Its normal operating pressure range is 6 to 10 bar. Rated pressure is a specification limit, not a recommended operating setpoint.

PMP-104 uses a mechanical seal to limit leakage around its rotating shaft. Seal inspection and replacement intervals are described in the separate maintenance guide.

This educational specification does not state the motor power, motor speed, or electrical supply. Those properties cannot be inferred from the pressure rating.

pages.title: PMP-104: Pressure Monitoring
pages.text:
The pressure sensor PRS-204 monitors pump PMP-104. The illustrative high-pressure alarm threshold is 9 bar. An alarm is a reason to review the inspection record, not proof that the pump or sensor has failed.

A measured pressure within the normal operating range does not prove that all components are healthy. Pressure and seal condition are separate observations. Consult the maintenance guide for inspection intervals.

pages.title: PMP-104: Seal Inspection
pages.text:
For fictional pump PMP-104, inspect the mechanical seal every 30 days. Record visible leakage and seal condition in the inspection record. This interval is not determined by the pump's 12 bar rated pressure.

The illustrative scheduled seal replacement interval is 1,000 operating hours. Visible damage requires a separate maintenance review; this sample does not authorize continued operation or prescribe a repair procedure.

pages.title: PRS-204: Sensor Review
pages.text:
For the fictional pressure sensor PRS-204 on pump PMP-104, the calibration review interval is 90 days. Review an alarm alongside the measured pressure and maintenance history before assigning a cause.

The inspection record contains observations, not a fault diagnosis. Elevated vibration alone does not establish that the mechanical seal or pressure sensor caused it. This guide supplies no vibration limit or diagnostic procedure.

pages.title: PMP-104: Inspection Record
pages.text:
Fictional inspection record 01 for pump PMP-104. The recorded pressure was 8.2 bar. The mechanical seal had no visible leakage at the time of inspection.

The operator recorded elevated vibration. No cause was established. The record contains no motor power measurement and does not certify the equipment as safe.

This page is an image-only scan created for testing OCR. Its contents were authored for the ConceptGraph demonstration, not collected from real equipment.

pages.title: Interpreting the Record
pages.text:
To interpret inspection record 01 for PMP-104, compare its measured pressure with the operating range in equipment-specification.pdf. Compare its seal observation with the inspection requirements in equipment-maintenance.pdf.

The specification, guide, and inspection record describe different facts. An observation does not override a specification, and a maintenance interval is not an inspection result. Use the cited pages rather than treating these documents as interchangeable.

saved_examples.question: What is PMP-104's pressure rating, and how often should its seal be inspected?
saved_examples.answer: The specification gives PMP-104 a rated pressure of 12 bar and a normal operating range of 6 to 10 bar. The separate maintenance guide specifies a seal inspection every 30 days. The pressure rating is not an inspection interval or operating setpoint; both documents are needed to answer this question.
